2.content:
Google’s Silicon COT Supply Chain Process Implementation is an 18-month, phased engagement to implement a silicon Customer Owned Tooling supply chain using SAP S/4HANA, Kinaxis, and E2Open, enabling end-to-end manufacturing traceability, partner collaboration, and yield-aware supply planning across Google’s silicon operations.

- Establish the target-state silicon supply chain design through AS-IS assessment, TO-BE finalization, and phased solution delivery across procurement, manufacturing operations, quality, logistics, finance, planning, and organizational change management.
- Configure and integrate SAP S/4HANA, Kinaxis, and E2Open to support material master, batch and lot traceability, production planning, constrained supply planning, and collaboration with TSMC and OSAT partners.
- Deliver business go-live in April 2027 and scale the solution through December 2027 to expand manufacturing visibility, analytical capability, and operational adoption.

Deferred scope decisions, delivery assumptions, and dependency conditions are set out in Section 10 (Key Assumptions) and Section 21 (Key Observations).

3.1.content:
Google is implementing a silicon Customer Owned Tooling supply chain to replace limited, fragmented visibility across foundry, OSAT, planning, and enterprise processes with an integrated operating model. The current state requires clearer baseline understanding of core PO flows, material master setup, batch and lot traceability, subcontracting settlement, E2Open collaboration, enterprise structure, and partner connectivity for TSMC and OSAT operations.

The engagement is driven by the need to establish end-to-end manufacturing traceability, improve partner collaboration, support constrained and yield-aware supply planning, and strengthen the ASIC commit process. Google intends to deliver this through a phased program using SAP S/4HANA, Kinaxis, and E2Open across procurement, manufacturing operations, quality, finance, logistics, trade compliance, planning, and organizational change management, with business go-live targeted for April 2027 and scale-out through December 2027.

3.2.content:
- Establish the AS-IS baseline for silicon front-end and back-end supply chain processes, systems, data flows, and organizational structure.
- Finalize the TO-BE design for the silicon COT operating model across SAP S/4HANA, Kinaxis, and E2Open.
- Enable manufacturing visibility across foundry and OSAT partners, including batch and lot traceability.
- Configure core PP and MM processes to support material master, production planning, subcontracting, goods movements, and process execution.
- Integrate SAP S/4HANA, Kinaxis, and E2Open to support planning, collaboration, and transactional data flow.
- Deliver TSMC PO capability by December 4, 2026 and achieve business go-live in April 2027.
- Expand the solution through 2027 to add broader analytical capability, operational adoption, and scaled process coverage.

3.3.content: The target-state process begins with demand and supply planning in Kinaxis, with approved planning signals driving procurement and execution in SAP S/4HANA. Purchase orders, forecasts, commits, and partner collaboration messages are exchanged through E2Open to support foundry and OSAT coordination. Manufacturing execution progresses from wafer fabrication through probe, die bank, assembly, test, and finished goods, with batch and lot traceability maintained across the flow. Goods receipts, inventory visibility, subcontracting transactions, quality-relevant events, and planning updates are synchronized across the application landscape to provide a consistent view of supply, yield, and material status for Google and its manufacturing partners.

4.1.content: The engagement covers Google’s silicon Customer Owned Tooling supply chain operations across the United States, India, and Taiwan. Operational scope includes Google hub and warehouse locations, foundry operations at TSMC, and OSAT operations at KYEC and SPIL. Phase 1 and Phase 2 manufacturing scope is limited to Taiwan-based manufacturing flows. International mid-stream flows are excluded until Phase 3 expanded scope. Delivery will be performed through a blended onshore and offshore model from approved Google and Bristlecone delivery locations.

4.2.content: In-scope business processes include Customer Owned Tooling process implementation and the end-to-end silicon supply chain flow required to support manufacturing visibility, partner collaboration, and yield-aware supply planning. This includes AS-IS assessment, fit-gap analysis, and TO-BE process finalization for procurement, production planning, materials management, manufacturing operations, subcontracting, goods movements, batch and lot traceability, quality-relevant process events, inventory visibility, and partner collaboration across foundry and OSAT operations. The scope also includes constrained supply planning, inventory planning, analytics and reporting, and process improvements supporting the overall ASIC commit process.

4.3.content: Technical scope includes configuration of SAP S/4HANA for silicon manufacturing processes within PP and MM, design and configuration of Kinaxis for supply, constraint, and inventory planning, and enablement of E2Open-based partner collaboration. Integration scope includes SAP S/4HANA, Kinaxis, and E2Open data flows using Google’s existing integration framework, with incremental delta interfaces analyzed during discovery and delivered where required. The solution will leverage existing data templates and modify them for silicon planning requirements, including additional inbound data for capacity and contract manufacturing data from TSMC, KYEC, and SPIL. Technical scope also includes functional specifications for approved custom development, data migration support, test assets, cutover support, and hypercare stabilization.

4.4.content: Included services are project management, fit-gap analysis, AS-IS assessment, TO-BE process design, business process design documentation, solution configuration and build, functional specification development for approved custom development, test planning and execution, unit testing, system integration testing, user acceptance testing support, regression testing, performance testing, data migration support, cutover planning and execution, hypercare, organization change management, train-the-trainer support, and knowledge transfer to the support team. Delivery will follow a phased Agile model aligned to Explore, Build, and Deploy stages.

4.5.content:
Application scope includes SAP S/4HANA, Kinaxis, and E2Open. Within SAP S/4HANA, in-scope functionality includes Production Planning and Materials Management required for the silicon COT operating model, including material master, production planning, subcontracting-relevant transactions, goods movements, and traceability support. Within Kinaxis, in-scope functionality includes supply planning, constraint planning, inventory planning, analytics and reporting, and required data integration. Within E2Open, in-scope functionality is limited to partner collaboration required to support foundry and OSAT coordination through the agreed silicon supply chain process.

5.content:
The solution architecture uses SAP S/4HANA as the execution backbone for silicon Customer Owned Tooling processes, Kinaxis as the planning orchestration layer for constrained supply and yield-aware planning, and E2Open for supplier collaboration with TSMC and OSAT partners. The design leverages Google’s existing integration framework where feasible and adds incremental interfaces required for silicon planning, manufacturing visibility, and partner connectivity.

<IMAGE id="72b8c9d44014"/>

The deployment model is phased and agile across Explore, Build, and Deploy. Explore establishes the AS-IS baseline, confirms the Silicon BU organizational structure, defines master and transactional data requirements, and finalizes integration boundaries across SAP S/4HANA, Kinaxis, E2Open, and downstream analytics. Build and Deploy progress through phased delivery of manufacturing visibility, technical go-live in January 2027, business go-live in April 2027, and scaling through December 2027.

Change governance will be managed through a wave-based delivery framework with integrated project management, integration, process, training, and change-management tracks. Governance will operate through weekly, bi-weekly, monthly, and quarterly reviews to track milestones, risks, dependencies, and cross-functional decisions across Google, Bristlecone, foundry, and OSAT stakeholders. Business process design will be completed before system configuration, and scope changes affecting integrations, analytics boundaries, or regional rollout will be routed through the formal change management process.

6.1.content:
Delivery will follow a phased Agile model across Explore, Build, and Deploy, with integrated SAP S/4HANA, Kinaxis, and E2Open workstreams. Explore covers mobilization, AS-IS assessment, fit-gap analysis, localization validation, solution mapping, design reviews, integration boundary confirmation, and update of the project plan, charter, governance structure, and RICEFW backlog. Build covers configuration, approved custom development, unit testing, mock data loads, security implementation, system integration testing, user acceptance testing support, training preparation, and readiness tracking. Deploy covers cutover planning, go/no-go decision support, end-user training, production go-live, hypercare, knowledge transfer, and project closure.

The rollout will be executed in waves aligned to Phase 1 foundation and manufacturing visibility, Phase 2 full MVP and business go-live, and Phase 3 scale-out. Delivery governance will combine weekly execution tracking with milestone-based decision reviews to manage dependencies, risks, data readiness, partner coordination, and scope changes.

7.1.content:
Project governance will operate through a tiered structure aligned to phased Agile delivery across Explore, Build, and Deploy. Executive Sponsors will provide strategic direction, funding alignment, and milestone decision support. The Google Solution Architect, Integration Lead, Key Business Users, and Functional Lead will govern solution design, data flow alignment, process validation, and business readiness. The Program Manager will lead day-to-day delivery governance, including plan tracking, dependency management, risk escalation, and cross-workstream coordination across Google and Bristlecone teams.

Working governance forums will include weekly execution reviews, design and integration working sessions, milestone readiness reviews, and monthly steering reviews. Escalations will move from workstream leads to the Program Manager, then to Google and Bristlecone leadership for decisions affecting scope, timeline, partner dependencies, or go-live readiness. Dependencies involving MES, PLM, other integrations, or local regulations will be tracked as formal governance items and escalated based on delivery impact.

10.content:
- Delivery is based on a phased Agile model across Explore, Build, and Deploy, with business go-live targeted for April 2027 and scale-out continuing through December 2027.
- TSMC purchase order capability will be live by December 4, 2026, and upstream planning, design, data, and integration decisions will be completed in time to support the 22-week fab runway.
- Phase 1 and Phase 2 manufacturing scope is limited to Taiwan-based flows across TSMC, KYEC, and SPIL; international mid-stream flows are excluded until Phase 3.
- Google’s existing integration framework will be retained where feasible, and only approved incremental delta interfaces identified during discovery are in scope.
- BOM explosion will be provided through PLM-managed sharing of GPNs and BOMs with contract manufacturing partners and can be leveraged by SAP S/4HANA and Kinaxis without material redesign by Bristlecone.
- CO/FICO staffing and delivery remain Google responsibilities, and material valuation, costing, and yield accounting are not part of Bristlecone’s scope.
- TMS, EWM, Commercial Invoice APIs, Silicon Data Hub net new integrations, and manufacturing collaboration integrations beyond the agreed E2Open-based scope are excluded unless added through the Change Management Process.
- Google will provide timely access to business process owners, IT leads, core users, and partner-facing stakeholders needed for design reviews, testing, training, cutover, and sign-off.
- Google will confirm the agreed inventory ownership transition points, including the assumption that Google owns WIP after probe completion at TSMC and ownership transfers at goods receipt.
- Any change to phased scope boundaries, milestone dates, integration volumes, partner coverage, ownership assumptions, or excluded functional areas will be managed through the Change Management Process described in Section 17.

16.1.content:
Milestone governance for this engagement will be managed through the Key Deliverables and Commercials sections. Each major phase deliverable will be tied to its scheduled milestone, acceptance criteria, responsible party, and the applicable monthly fixed fee milestone or phase-specific commercial amount.

Phase 1 governance will track Foundation activities in Q2–Q3 2026 and Manufacturing Visibility delivery through the December 4, 2026 TSMC PO milestone. Phase 2 governance will track Full MVP readiness through January 25, 2027, technical go-live in January 2027, business go-live in April 2027, and hypercare through Q2 2027. Phase 3 governance will track scale-out, expanded analytical capability, and scaling activities from April through December 2027.

<IMAGE id="960380ff376b"/>

The Program Manager will maintain milestone status, dependencies, and sign-off readiness, and will escalate any variance affecting committed dates, deliverables, or commercial milestones through the governance model.

16.2.content:
- WMS, TMS, and Commercial Invoice API scope will remain excluded unless confirmed and approved through change control.
- International mid-stream flows will remain out of scope for Phase 1 and Phase 2 and may be evaluated as part of Phase 3 expanded scope.
- Additional partner connectivity, manufacturing collaboration expansion, and net new Silicon Data Hub integrations are deferred unless separately approved.
- Incremental delta interfaces identified during discovery will be baselined before build and treated as scope additions if they exceed the agreed integration boundary.
- Google-owned decisions affecting WIP ownership transfer, CO/FICO support dependencies, and cross-team readiness must be finalized in line with project milestones to avoid schedule impact.

16.3.content:
- The approved baseline integration scope is limited to SAP S/4HANA, Kinaxis, and E2Open interfaces required for the silicon COT process.
- Existing Google integration framework will be retained where feasible; only incremental delta interfaces confirmed through discovery and approved for delivery will be built.
- Net new integrations beyond the agreed scope, including Silicon Data Hub expansion or additional partner connectivity, require formal scope approval before design or build starts.
- Custom development will be limited to approved functional specifications and the finalized RICEFW backlog.
- Any increase in interface volume, custom object scope, reporting scope, or partner onboarding that affects effort, timeline, or cost will be routed through the Change Management Process.
- Integration design, data mapping, loading, and validation activities must be completed in line with phase readiness gates before SIT, UAT, cutover, and go-live.
- The hard deadline for TSMC PO capability on December 4, 2026 will take precedence in sequencing decisions for integration and build activities.

16.4.content:
All changes to scope, timeline, deliverables, integration boundaries, custom development, staffing assumptions, delivery locations, or commercials will be governed through the Change Management Process set out in Section 17.

No work outside the approved baseline will proceed without documented impact assessment and written approval. Each change request will record the requested change, delivery impact, dependency impact, acceptance impact, and any adjustment to milestone timing or fees. Approved changes will be reflected in the applicable SOW amendment, addendum, revised deliverable plan, or commercial schedule before execution. Unapproved backlog items, parking-lot items, and discovery findings will not be treated as committed scope until they complete that process.

17.content:
All changes to scope, timeline, deliverables, integrations, commercials, or agreed assumptions shall be managed through a formal Change Request process. No work outside the approved baseline will proceed without written approval from Google and Bristlecone.

| Step | Activity | Owner | Timeline |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | CR raised | Either party identifies a requested change, documents the proposed change, business rationale, and affected scope, and submits the Change Request to the Program Manager. | Google or Bristlecone requestor | Within 2 business days of identifying the change |
| 2 | CR logged | The Change Request is recorded in the project change log, assigned a tracking ID, and categorized by scope, timeline, cost, integration, data, or dependency impact. | Bristlecone Program Manager | Within 1 business day of receipt |
| 3 | Impact assessment | Affected functional, technical, integration, testing, data, and change-management leads assess delivery impact, milestone effect, commercial impact, and dependency risk, including impact to the December 4, 2026 TSMC PO milestone, January 2027 technical go-live, and April 2027 business go-live where applicable. | Bristlecone Program Manager with Google solution, integration, and business leads | Within 5 business days of logging |
| 4 | CR reviewed / approved | The assessed Change Request is reviewed in the agreed governance forum and approved, rejected, or deferred. Changes affecting cost, contractual scope, or committed milestone dates require authorized approval from both parties. | Google and Bristlecone authorized approvers | Within 5 business days of impact assessment completion |
| 5 | SOW amendment / addendum | Approved changes requiring contractual updates are reflected through an amendment, addendum, or written commercial authorization before execution of the changed work. Project plans, deliverables, and baselines are updated accordingly. | Google and Bristlecone authorized approvers with project management support | Before execution of approved changed work |
| 6 | CR closure | After implementation or formal disposition, the Change Request status, decision, approval evidence, and resulting baseline updates are recorded and the CR is closed in the change log. | Bristlecone Program Manager | Within 2 business days of implementation or final decision |

Changes driven by additional interfaces, expanded partner connectivity, scope beyond agreed exclusions, or deviation from Section 10 assumptions shall follow this process. Emergency decisions needed to protect a committed milestone may be escalated through the project governance structure for expedited review, but still require formal logging and approval.

19.1.content: Either party may terminate this SOW for convenience by giving <LEGAL: required notice period under the governing agreement, or if silent, agreed written notice period> prior written notice to the other party. 19.2.content: Either party may terminate this SOW for cause upon written notice if the other party materially breaches this SOW and fails to cure that breach within the cure period stated in the governing agreement. A party may also terminate for cause if the other party becomes insolvent, enters liquidation or bankruptcy proceedings, ceases to conduct business in the ordinary course, or engages in fraud, willful misconduct, or unlawful activity affecting performance under this SOW. 19.3.content: On termination or expiration of this SOW, Bristlecone will stop performing the terminated Services as of the effective date of termination, except for agreed transition or wind-down activities. Google will pay Bristlecone for Services properly performed through the termination date, including earned fixed monthly milestone fees, approved change requests already executed, and pre-approved reimbursable travel and expenses incurred before termination. Each party will promptly return or securely destroy the other party’s Confidential Information in accordance with the governing agreement and applicable policy. Any Google systems, environments, credentials, badges, or access rights provided to Bristlecone personnel for this engagement will be revoked or returned. Termination of this SOW will not affect rights or obligations that by their nature survive termination, including payment obligations accrued before termination, confidentiality, audit rights, limitation of liability, and dispute resolution, to the extent provided in the governing agreement.
